title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and the six Bengali seasons, say how hot or cold you feel, and predict what the weather is going to do.
intro:
Bengal traditionally has **six seasons** (ষড়ঋতু), each two months long: গ্রীষ্ম (summer), বর্ষা (monsoon), শরৎ (early autumn), হেমন্ত (late autumn), শীত (winter) and বসন্ত (spring). In daily life people talk mostly about গরম, বর্ষা and শীত, and endlessly about the rain.

Weather in Bengali isn't 'it is raining' but '**rain is happening / falling**' (বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে / পড়ছে), '**sun has risen**' (রোদ উঠেছে), '**wind is giving**' (হাওয়া দিচ্ছে). Each weather word has its favourite verb.

vocab.note: Season of Durga Puja, white কাশফুল and blue skies.

phrases.en: It looks like it's going to rain.
Winter has come late this year.

phrases.native: তোমার কোন ঋতু সবচেয়ে ভালো লাগে?
phrases.roman: tomar kon ritu shôbcheye bhalo lage?
phrases.en: Which season do you like best?

grammar.title: Weather expressions: each word has its verb
grammar.body:
English uses a dummy 'it' (*it's raining*). Bengali makes the weather itself the subject, with a typical verb:

**বৃষ্টি হওয়া / পড়া** – rain happens / falls: বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে, বৃষ্টি পড়ছে
**রোদ ওঠা** – sun rises: রোদ উঠেছে 'it's sunny'
**হাওয়া দেওয়া** – wind gives: হাওয়া দিচ্ছে 'it's windy'
**গরম / শীত পড়া** – heat / cold falls: খুব গরম পড়েছে 'it's very hot (these days)'
**মেঘ করা** – cloud makes: মেঘ করেছে 'it's clouded over'
**ঝড় ওঠা / আসা** – storm rises / comes

How **you** feel uses the experiencer pattern: **আমার শীত করছে / লাগছে** 'I feel cold', **আমার গরম লাগছে** 'I feel hot'.

examples.en: It rained all night last night.
It gets very cold in January.
Turn the fan on, I'm feeling hot.

grammar.title: 'It's going to…': future + মনে হচ্ছে, হতে পারে
grammar.body:
To predict, use the **future tense** (unit 17 covers it in full; for now: **হবে** 'will happen', **আসবে** 'will come', **থামবে** 'will stop').

**মনে হচ্ছে** 'it seems' + future = 'it looks like it's going to…': মনে হচ্ছে বৃষ্টি হবে.
**হয়তো** 'perhaps' + future: হয়তো কাল ঝড় হবে.
**-তে পারে** 'may, might' (infinitive + পারা): বৃষ্টি হতে পারে 'it might rain'.
**-তে যাচ্ছে** 'is about to' is heard in modern speech: বৃষ্টি নামতে যাচ্ছে.

The forecast word is **পূর্বাভাস** (formal); in everyday speech people say আবহাওয়ার খবর 'weather news'.

examples.en: It looks like it's going to rain today.
There may be a storm in the afternoon.
It's going to get cold from tomorrow.

dialogue.title: Caught in the monsoon
dialogue.setting: Two colleagues, Anil and Sophie, look out of the office window in Kolkata in July.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.native: দেখো, আকাশটা কী কালো হয়ে গেছে!
lines.roman: dækho, akashṭa ki kalo hoye gechhe!
lines.en: Look, how dark the sky has become!

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.native: হ্যাঁ, মনে হচ্ছে জোরে বৃষ্টি আসবে।
lines.roman: hæṃ, mone hochchhe jore brishṭi ashbe.
lines.en: Yes, it looks like heavy rain is coming.

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.native: চিন্তা কোরো না, আমার কাছে দুটো আছে।
lines.roman: chinta koro na, amar kachhe duṭo achhe.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.native: বর্ষায় কি রোজ এরকম বৃষ্টি হয়?
lines.roman: bôrshay ki roj ærôkom brishṭi hôy?
lines.en: Does it rain like this every day in the monsoon?

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.native: প্রায় রোজই। রাস্তায় জলও জমে যায়।
lines.roman: pray roji. rastay jôlo jome jay.
lines.en: Almost every day. The roads flood too.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.en: But at least the heat has gone down a bit.

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.native: ঠিক। আর শরৎকালে আকাশ একদম নীল হয়ে যায়।
lines.roman: ṭhik. ar shôrotkale akash ækdôm nil hoye jay.
lines.en: True. And in autumn the sky turns completely blue.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.native: চলো, বৃষ্টি থামলে চা খেতে যাই।
lines.roman: chôlo, brishṭi thamle cha khete jai.
lines.en: Let's go for tea when the rain stops.

culture: The monsoon (বর্ষা) is the most celebrated season in Bengali poetry and song: Tagore wrote over a hundred rain songs. A rainy day calls for খিচুড়ি (rice-and-lentil porridge) and fried ইলিশ. Bangladesh is a delta of hundreds of rivers, and floods and cyclones are a real part of life; weather warnings use signal numbers (e.g. ১০ নম্বর মহাবিপদ সংকেত 'danger signal no. 10').

tip.title: The weather has its own verb
tip.body:
- No dummy 'it': the weather word is the subject, with its own verb.
- বৃষ্টি **হচ্ছে / পড়ছে** 'it's raining', রোদ **উঠেছে** 'the sun's out', হাওয়া **দিচ্ছে** 'it's windy', মেঘ **করেছে** 'it's clouded over'.
- Learn each pair as one chunk: you can't say রোদ দিচ্ছে or হাওয়া উঠেছে.
tip.pattern: বৃষ্টি + হচ্ছে  ·  রোদ + উঠেছে  ·  হাওয়া + দিচ্ছে

sentences.en: It's raining outside.
The sun's out after many days.
It's very windy today.
Look, it's clouded over.
It rained a lot yesterday.
It's not raining, it's just cloudy.
Here it rains every afternoon.
What's the weather like in Dhaka?
The weather's lovely today.
What lovely sunshine!

tip.title: আমার শীত করছে: I feel cold
tip.body:
- How *you* feel takes **আমার**, not আমি: **আমার** শীত করছে / লাগছে 'I feel cold', **আমার** গরম লাগছে 'I feel hot'.
- The weather itself 'falls': শীত **পড়েছে** 'it's turned cold', গরম **পড়েছে** 'it's hot these days'.
- Got wet: **ভিজে গেছি**; wet **ভেজা**, dry **শুকনো**.

sentences.en: Are you cold?
I'm feeling really hot.
I'm not cold.
It's turned really cold this year.
It gets very hot at midday.
It doesn't snow in our country.
My shirt got wet in the rain.
It was very foggy this morning.

sentences.native: জামাটা ভেজা, একটা শুকনো জামা দাও।
sentences.roman: jamaṭa bheja, ækṭa shukno jama dao.
sentences.en: This shirt's wet, give me a dry one.
Could you put a little ice in the water?

tip.title: 'It's going to…', 'it might…'
tip.body:
- To predict, use the future: **হবে** 'will happen', **আসবে** 'will come', **থামবে** 'will stop'.
- **মনে হচ্ছে** + future = 'it looks like…': মনে হচ্ছে ঝড় **আসবে**.
- **-তে পারে** = 'might': বৃষ্টি **হতে পারে** 'it might rain'.

sentences.en: It looks like a storm's coming this afternoon.
It might rain tomorrow.
Will the rain stop?

sentences.native: আকাশ পরিষ্কার, আজ বৃষ্টি হবে না।
sentences.roman: akash porishkar, aj brishṭi hobe na.
sentences.en: The sky's clear, it won't rain today.
Take an umbrella, it might rain.
It looks like the sun will come out.
It will get cooler from tomorrow.
You can't see the sun today.
How lovely the moon is tonight!

sentences.native: আকাশে মেঘ নেই, ছাতা লাগবে না।
sentences.roman: akashe megh nei, chhata lagbe na.
sentences.en: There are no clouds, you won't need an umbrella.

lessons.title: The six seasons

tip.title: Six seasons, and "in" a season
tip.body:
- Bengal counts **six** ঋতু: গ্রীষ্ম (গরমকাল), বর্ষা, শরৎ, হেমন্ত, শীত, বসন্ত.
- 'In' a season takes **-এ / -য়** or **-কালে**: **বর্ষায়**, **শীতে**, **বসন্তে**, **গরমকালে**.
- 'Which season do you like?' is an experiencer sentence: **তোমার** কোন ঋতু ভালো লাগে?

new: তোমার কোন ঋতু সবচেয়ে ভালো লাগে?

sentences.native: বর্ষায় আমি বাইরে বেশি যাই না।
sentences.roman: bôrshay ami baire beshi jai na.
sentences.en: In the monsoon I don't go out much.
I like early autumn best.
Kolkata is lovely in winter.
In spring the weather is really pleasant.

sentences.native: গরমকালে আমরা দুপুরে বাইরে যাই না।
sentences.roman: gôromkale amra dupure baire jai na.
sentences.en: In summer we don't go out at midday.
In late autumn there's a little fog in the mornings.
Do you like the monsoon?
Bengal has six seasons.
The monsoon came late this year.

sentences.native: আমাদের গ্রামে একটা বড় নদী আছে।
sentences.roman: amader grame ækṭa bôṛo nodi achhe.
sentences.en: There's a big river in our village.

sentences.native: আমার পাহাড়ের চেয়ে সমুদ্র বেশি ভালো লাগে।
sentences.roman: amar pahaṛer cheye shomudro beshi bhalo lage.
sentences.en: I like the sea more than the hills.
It's very cold in the hills now.
This tree's flowers are lovely.
The ground stays wet in the monsoon.
There are very few trees in the city.
I love nature.
We'll go to the village for the holidays.
The river is close to here.

sentences.native: সমুদ্রে এখন নামবেন না, ঝড় আসছে।
sentences.roman: shomudre ækhon namben na, jhôṛ ashchhe.
sentences.en: Don't go into the sea now, a storm's coming.
